smell_elimination.justification: The refactoring merely moves the deeply inlined code into separate helper methods but preserves all the manual protocol implementation. The core smell—manual depth tracking, exception capturing, and resource management—remains completely intact, just relocated. No abstraction layers are restored; the code still doesn't use context managers.

cross_file_coordination.justification: Changes are confined to core.py. The _setup_main_invocation helper from utils.py is still used but not modified. No orphaned code is created, but the refactoring also doesn't address any cross-file concerns that would genuinely improve the architecture.

structural_soundness.justification: The extraction into _parse_args_with_context and _invoke_with_context provides some organizational benefit, but both methods still violate single responsibility by mixing concern-level logic with low-level protocol implementation. The abstraction boundaries remain broken—these helpers still manually implement __enter__/__exit__ semantics.

code_quality.justification: The extraction makes Command.main() shorter and slightly more readable at first glance, but the helper methods are still dense with manual state management, depth tracking, and exception handling logic. The code is marginally easier to navigate but not easier to understand or maintain. Variable naming with underscores persists.

fragment_identification.justification: The refactoring correctly identifies the two major inlined fragments (parse phase and invoke phase) and the shell completion logic. Each is extracted to its own method. However, it fails to recognize that these fragments should be de-inlined by restoring context manager usage, not just moved wholesale.

extraction_quality.justification: While fragments are extracted into separate methods, the extraction quality is poor because each extracted method still contains the deeply inlined logic at the wrong abstraction level. _parse_args_with_context and _invoke_with_context still manually implement context lifecycle management instead of delegating to context managers. This is code motion, not proper de-inlining.

context_manager_restoration.justification: This is the most critical failure. The refactoring does not restore context manager usage at all. Both _parse_args_with_context and _invoke_with_context still contain manual _ctx._depth manipulation, explicit push_context/pop_context calls, exception tracking variables (_pfail, _iexc, _suppressed), and manual _close_with_exception_info() coordination. The entire manual __enter__/__exit__ implementation remains, just relocated to helper methods. No 'with' statements are introduced.

aspect_3_judge.summary: This refactoring is superficial window-dressing that fails to address the core smell. It extracts inlined code into helper methods, making Command.main() shorter, but preserves all the manual context manager protocol implementation—depth tracking, exception capturing, resource cleanup—that constitutes the deep inlining smell. The abstraction violation remains unaddressed; the code still implements __enter__/__exit__ logic manually instead of using Python's context manager protocol.
